We need answer only valid JSON. Need produce concise architecture plan at most 2000 words. Need include keys exactly: state_machine, timer_plan, priorities, initial_values, scan_execution_order explicit 4-stage, formal_assertions optional list id formula. Need ensure valid JSON. No markdown.

We need design PLC architecture for PUB012. Need account requirements. Need state machine list states/transitions. Timer plan timers PT durations reset conditions. Priorities safety/operational. Initial values. Scan execution order explicit 4-stage. Formal assertions over declared VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT port names. We can include assertions derived LTL using port names. Need be concise. Need mention internal variables maybe state. Need JSON only.

Need think architecture. We need model for alarm hold 500ms, fault counter/history, runtime accumulator. Inputs: THICKNESS_FAULT, THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID, CUTTING_RUN, FaultTimestamp DINT, CycleTime TIME. Outputs: THICKNESS_ALARM BOOL, Slab_Fault_Counter UINT, Slab_Runtime_Accumulator LTIME, Slab_Fault_History ARRAY[0..4] OF DINT.

Need precise semantics: rising edge of valid fault (valid AND fault AND NOT previous(valid AND fault)). On each false-to-true transition of valid fault signal? Requirement says "On each FALSE-to-TRUE transition of a valid fault signal, increment ...". Assumptions: counted signal is valid AND fault; a valid fault after signal loss is a new occurrence. So edge detection on validFault = THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID AND THICKNESS_FAULT. If invalid then previous validFault resets false? Important: validFault after signal loss is new occurrence. If we update prev_valid_fault = validFault every scan, when invalid prev becomes false, then when valid fault later true it's rising. Good. Need no spurious record when invalid. Edge sampling stage computes R_TRIG? Could use internal prevValidFault. Need decide scan order: 1 edge sampling (sample inputs, compute edge flags based on previous state?), 2 safety/reset priority & state transitions, 3 unconditional top-level timer FB calls outside CASE/IF, 4 unified output assignments. Need mention timer FB calls outside CASE/IF. We can define state machine maybe S0_INVALID, S1_MONITOR_IDLE? Better.

Need SAFETY: invalid signal overrides hold. On invalid: alarm off, hold state clear, timer reset, no records/runtime. At power-up init. Need clear holding state whenever invalid. If valid fault persistent, alarm on. If valid fault rising: start hold timer 500ms; alarm on. If fault absent and hold timer <500ms: alarm remains on. If hold expires and no fault: alarm off. If fresh rising trigger restarts hold. If fault persists, alarm on regardless timer. Timer reset conditions: invalid input resets; on rising valid fault restart PT 500ms; maybe reset when not needed? Need timer FB called unconditionally. Use TON? Need careful: TON timing: IN TRUE starts. We need hold timer active (<500ms since last valid rising fault edge) while valid. We can use TON with IN = valid AND validFaultEdge? But to measure hold from rising edge and continue after edge, need an internal hold active latch. Could use TON where IN = valid AND (holdActive OR validFaultEdge?) Actually TON PT=500ms; Q true after 500ms. Need hold if timer not Q and maybe since last edge. We can set holdActive as state until timer Q. But if fault absent, hold remains until timer Q. If fault present, alarm on. If fresh rising edge restarts timer: reset TON by setting IN false one scan? In IEC TON restart when IN false then true? If IN remains true, TON doesn't restart. Need handle fresh rising edge during active hold restart 500ms. If using TON with IN = valid AND holdActive, to restart at rising edge while already true, need reset timer FB or use timer reset. Could do stage: on validFaultRise set holdActive TRUE and call TON with IN maybe? To restart TON, need set IN false momentarily? In PLC scan, cannot easily call twice? Can use TON with IN = valid AND holdActive AND NOT restartPulse? Hmm.

Alternative use explicit elapsed time accumulator with CycleTime? The specification says hold at least 500ms. Timer_plan expects timers. But we can implement with TON and reset via state. Need design robust.

Given scan order: Stage 3 unconditional timer FB calls outside CASE/IF. We can have timer instance e.g. AlarmHoldTimer TON. Stage 2 sets a boolean `holdTimerEnable` maybe. Stage 3 calls TON unconditionally with IN := holdTimerEnable, PT := T#500ms. But to restart on fresh edge, need ensure holdTimerEnable goes false for at least one call before true. If edge occurs while holdTimerEnable already true, TON won't restart. Could use `holdTimerEnable := valid AND (validFaultRise OR (holdActive AND NOT AlarmHoldTimer.Q))`? At edge true, if already true, no restart. We need reset. Better use `holdActive` state and timer `AlarmHoldTimer` with IN := valid AND holdActive AND NOT resetHoldTimer. Stage 2 can set `resetHoldTimer` TRUE for one scan on rising edge to force IN false? But if we call TON with IN := valid AND holdActive AND NOT resetHoldTimer, then when resetHoldTimer true, timer resets, Q false, elapsed zero. Next scan reset false, IN true if holdActive, timer starts from zero. That gives one scan delay, still okay? At edge scan, timer reset. Alarm still on due fault. Hold minimum from edge? It restarts next scan, so effective hold from edge to expiry ~500ms + one scan. Meets at least 500ms. If fault absent after edge? Rising edge implies fault true in current scan, so alarm on due fault. If next scan fault false, holdActive true, timer started previous? Actually on edge scan, we set resetHoldTimer true, timer reset. Next scan fault false, holdActive remains, reset false, timer IN true starts. Hold expiry after 500ms from next scan. Slight ≥. Good.

But if fresh edge during active hold and fault persists, reset timer. Good. Need stage 2 determine reset. Or use `AlarmHoldTimer(IN := valid AND holdActive AND NOT holdRestart, PT := T#500ms);` Stage 2 sets holdRestart based edge. Need then after stage 3, Stage 2 state? In scan order, state transitions before timer calls. Timer Q is from previous scan? But TON called stage 3 updates Q same scan, output assignments stage 4 can use updated Q. Good. Need maybe if timer Q true, later stage? In state transitions stage 2 uses previous timer Q, but output stage uses current Q. Could have holdActive cleared in next scan after Q. That's fine, alarm output stage uses fault OR (holdActive AND NOT Q?) Need ensure release at 500ms if fault absent. If holdActive remains true but Q true, output alarm = valid AND (fault OR (holdActive AND NOT AlarmHoldTimer.Q)). At Q true and no fault alarm off. Next scan stage 2 clears holdActive if timer Q. Good.

Could also avoid complex state machine by dataflow. But required state_machine list. Define states:
- S_INIT / S_POWER_UP: initialize counters/history/runtime/alarm/hold/edge memory.
- S_INVALID: when THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID FALSE. Alarm OFF, hold inactive, timer reset, prevValidFault FALSE, no record/runtime. Transition to S_MONITOR_VALID when valid TRUE.
- S_MONITOR_VALID: valid TRUE. Subconditions:
  - validFault = valid AND fault.
  - validFaultRise -> record fault, restart hold, alarm on.
  - persistent fault -> alarm on, hold maybe maintain/restart? Requirement: hold each triggered alarm for at least 500ms; persistent fault keeps alarm. If fault persists longer than 500ms, timer may expire but alarm still on due fault. If fresh rising trigger occurs? If fault stays true no new edge. If fault drops then rises while hold active, restart.
  - fault absent and hold active until timer 500ms -> alarm on. When timer Q and no fault -> hold cleared, alarm off.
  - normal runtime if valid AND no fault AND CUTTING_RUN -> add CycleTime. Note no fault (not validFault) regardless hold. If alarm hold active but no fault, still normal? Requirement: accumulate while CUTTING_RUN TRUE, signal valid and no thickness fault present. So if fault absent, even alarm hold active due previous fault, runtime accumulates. Yes normal = valid & !fault & CUTTING_RUN. No alarm condition in runtime. Good.
  - transitions to S_INVALID on invalid.

Maybe state machine list with states and transitions objects. Could include internal pseudo-state for hold? Better define states: S_POWER_UP, S_SIGNAL_INVALID, S_VALID_NO_FAULT, S_VALID_FAULT, S_HOLD_AFTER_FAULT. But alarm hold and fault can overlap. State machine may have composite. Need not exhaustive. Need list of states and transitions. Could include states:
- S0_POWER_UP_INIT
- S1_SIGNAL_INVALID
- S2_VALID_NORMAL (valid, no fault, no hold)
- S3_VALID_FAULT (valid, fault true; alarm forced)
- S4_VALID_HOLD (valid, no fault, hold timer active)
Transitions:
S0 -> S1 if !valid else S2? At first scan maybe init then evaluate. Could be transition unconditional to S1/S2 based valid. But state machine can start S0, exit after init. Or omit S0? Need include init.
S1 invalid -> S1 while !valid; -> S2 when valid & !fault; -> S3 when valid & fault (rising? persistent? if valid fault true). Also on entering S1: alarm false, hold reset, prevValidFault false.
S2 -> S3 on valid & fault (edge record if prev false); -> S1 on !valid; -> S2 normal runtime if CUTTING_RUN; no alarm.
S3 -> S1 on !valid; -> S4 on valid & !fault (hold active started at last rise); -> S3 persistent fault; if? Could transition from S3 to S2 if fault absent and hold expired? But on fault absent, hold active for 500ms, so S4. If hold already expired? Fault just absent and hold? Since fault persistent, timer may have expired. When fault drops, should alarm maybe? Requirement: hold each triggered alarm for at least 500ms. If fault persisted >500ms, then when fault drops, is alarm required to hold further? "hold each triggered alarm for at least 500 ms. Keep the alarm active while the fault persists." If fault persisted 1s, alarm has been active >500ms, so on drop can turn off immediately? The assumption says "Hold starts at elapsed zero on the trigger call and releases at 500ms if the fault is absent. A fresh rising trigger restarts the hold." This implies if fault persists beyond 500ms, hold timer has expired; when fault absent, no hold remains, alarm releases immediately. But if using holdActive until timer Q, if timer already Q then on fault drop should go S2 (alarm off), not S4. Need state machine handle: from S3 with fault drop, if hold timer not expired, go S4; if expired go S2. But if persistent fault at rising, timer started. If after 500ms, Q true. Then fault drop: alarm off immediately because hold expired. That matches "releases at 500ms if fault absent" (if fault was present at 500ms, hold condition not relevant? Actually alarm remains due fault. At 500ms no fault? No. If fault absent exactly then release. If fault persists, timer expiration doesn't matter. When fault later drops, timer already expired, so no extra hold. Good.)
Need maybe state transitions:
S3_VALID_FAULT:
- if !valid -> S1
- if valid & fault -> S3 (persistent; alarm on; runtime no)
- if valid & !fault & AlarmHoldTimer.Q -> S2 (hold expired, alarm off)
- if valid & !fault & !AlarmHoldTimer.Q -> S4 (hold active; alarm on)
S4_VALID_HOLD:
- if !valid -> S1
- if valid & fault -> S3 (new or persistent? If fault returns/rises while hold active, edge record? Edge detection handles. Alarm on. If rising restart timer. If fault true but prev validFault false -> edge record. State S3.)
- if valid & !fault & !AlarmHoldTimer.Q -> S4 (hold)
- if valid & !fault & AlarmHoldTimer.Q -> S2 (release)
S2:
- if !valid -> S1
- if valid & fault -> S3
- if valid & !fault -> S2 (normal runtime if CUTTING_RUN)
But what about S3 persistent fault and timer Q true, if fault remains, stays S3. If fault drops, S2 immediately because Q true. Good.
What about S3 with fault true and timer not Q, timer may eventually Q; no state transition, stays S3. Alarm on due fault. If fault drops later after Q, go S2 immediately. Good.
What about S4 and new rising? If valid & fault true from no fault, transition S3 and edge record. If fault true while already fault? Not possible in S4 (no fault). Good.

Need edge detection: `validFault` previous. If invalid, prevValidFault reset FALSE. In S1, on entering set prevValidFault false. On valid fault after signal loss, edge true if prev false. Good.

Need record on rising validFault. In scan order: Stage 1 edge sampling uses previous `prevValidFault` (from last scan) and current inputs to produce `validFault`, `rise`. But if invalid, `validFault` false. Stage 2 on rise: increment counter, shift history (history[4]:=history[3]; ... history[0]:=FaultTimestamp). Need avoid record if invalid. rise = valid & fault & NOT prevValidFault. Good. Stage 2 also update prevValidFault? If update at stage 2 after edge, then edge sampling for next scan. But stage 1 already sampled. Need scan execution order explicit: Stage 1 edge sampling: sample inputs, compute validFault, rise using stored previous validFault; update previous validFault at end? Hmm edge sampling stage should maybe update previous after? But state transitions in stage 2 need rise. If we update prev in stage 1, then stage 2 can't compute? We can compute rise in stage 1 and store. Then stage 1 also set prevValidFault := validFault for next scan. But if invalid resets, good. However requirement stage 2 safety/reset & state transitions. If signal invalid, stage 1 still computes rise false because valid false. Stage 2 handles invalid. prevValidFault already false. Good. But if stage 1 updates prevValidFault before stage 2, and stage 2 invalid resets, same. Fine.
But if we want invalid input cancels hold immediately same observed scan, stage 2 does. Good.

Need runtime accumulation: Use `normal := valid AND NOT fault AND CUTTING_RUN`. "Positive CycleTime is added on every current qualifying call, including a normal first invocation." Need in scan stage 2 or 4? It's statistic update; stage 2 state transitions maybe includes stats under priority? But stage 4 unified output assignments. Could update in stage 2 under no invalid and no rise? Hmm. Need scan order: Stage 2 safety/reset & state transitions. Stats maybe in stage 2? But outputs assigned stage 4. We can compute internal accumulator updates in stage 2 (state/stat updates) then stage 4 assign outputs. Need ensure runtime add even on first normal invocation. Initial accumulator 0. On stage 2 if valid normal add CycleTime. If invalid, preserve? Requirement 5: At power-up initialize to zero. Requirement 3: accumulate while CUTTING_RUN, valid, no fault; otherwise preserve. Requirement 4: Do not accumulate normal runtime while signal invalid. So on invalid preserve accumulated value? Wait "Do not add fault records or accumulate normal runtime while signal is invalid." It doesn't say clear runtime each invalid. Requirement 5: At power-up initialize runtime zero. So invalid preserves previous accumulated runtime? Yes statistics accumulated; only reset at power-up. Requirement 1/4 "At power-up or whenever THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID is FALSE, switch off alarm and clear its holding state." Only alarm/hold, not runtime. So runtime preserved on invalid. Counter/history preserved on invalid. Good. Need initial only. Runtime add only if valid && !fault && CUTTING_RUN. CycleTime positive assumption. Use LTIME addition. Need mention if CycleTime <=0? Assumption positive. Could guard? We can ignore or guard to avoid negative. But not necessary. Maybe include `IF CycleTime > T#0ms`? Since TIME may signed? IEC TIME positive. Fine.

Need history readonly to callers: not a PLC mechanism, document as internal update only, no external write. In architecture, history output assigned from internal `Slab_Fault_History_Int` maybe? Or output array updated only stage 2. "External callers must not modify history entries." We can have internal `FaultHistory` that is copied to output in stage 4; only internal shift updates. But if output is same variable, callers could write? In PLC, output array may be writable by HMI? Architecture: maintain private `FaultHistory_Internal` and stage 4 copy to `Slab_Fault_History`. No code writes output except stage 4. Good. For counter/runtime similarly internal variables then output stage 4? Could. But output variables are likely writable. Need use internal state variables: `FaultCounter_Int`, `RuntimeAccumulator_Int`, `FaultHistory_Int`. Stage 4 assigns outputs. Initial values for internal and outputs. Need mention `prevValidFault`, `holdActive`, `AlarmHoldTimer`, `state`, maybe `validFaultRise`.

Need formal assertions. We can use LTL formulas over port names. The user says optional list of {"id": "A1", "formula": "G(...)"} temporal/invariant assertions over declared VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT port names. Need include maybe from given LTL but adapt to port names. Need ensure formulas are valid LTL string. Use `G(!THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID -> !THICKNESS_ALARM)`, `G(THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID & (THICKNESS_FAULT | hold) -> THICKNESS_ALARM)` but `hold` internal not port. The request says over declared VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT port names. So avoid internal hold? We can express observable properties using ports only:
- A1: G(!THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID -> !THICKNESS_ALARM)
- A2: G(THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID & THICKNESS_FAULT -> THICKNESS_ALARM) (persistent fault keeps alarm)
- A3: G((THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID & THICKNESS_FAULT & !X(THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID & THICKNESS_FAULT)) -> X(Slab_Fault_Counter = ...))? Can't refer pre-count easily. LTL over typed scan predicates can use `X` and previous? Need formulas can use `X`? Temporal. But comparing counter increment across scans requires arithmetic: `(Slab_Fault_Counter = X(Slab_Fault_Counter) - 1)`? Actually in LTL, next vs previous. We can write `G((THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID & THICKNESS_FAULT & !X(THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID & THICKNESS_FAULT)) -> X(Slab_Fault_Counter = ...))` not clean. Maybe assertions can be invariants about history read-only? Hmm. The user says optional. We can include simple invariants and safety. Need "over declared VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT port names" not necessarily all LTL from spec. Could include:
A1 `G(!THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID -> !THICKNESS_ALARM)`
A2 `G(THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID & THICKNESS_FAULT -> THICKNESS_ALARM)`
A3 `G((THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID & !THICKNESS_FAULT & !CUTTING_RUN) -> X(Slab_Runtime_Accumulator = Slab_Runtime_Accumulator))`? This says if not normal, next runtime same as current. But in LTL, `X(Slab_Runtime_Accumulator = Slab_Runtime_Accumulator)` compares next value to same current? Need previous operator. Actually within X, both refer next? In LTL, variables in X scope refer next state; `X(Slab_Runtime_Accumulator = Slab_Runtime_Accumulator)` is tautology. Need use `Slab_Runtime_Accumulator = X(Slab_Runtime_Accumulator)`? This means current equals next if condition holds? Formula `G((!THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID | THICKNESS_FAULT | !CUTTING_RUN) -> (Slab_Runtime_Accumulator = X(Slab_Runtime_Accumulator)))` But X in consequent only. This uses current and next. Good. However if condition holds at current scan, runtime should be same next? Wait runtime is updated during current scan based on current inputs. Observed outputs O[k] after call. If condition `!normal` at scan k, then O[k] runtime should equal previous runtime O[k-1]. In LTL, to express at scan k: `(normal@k -> runtime@k = runtime@(k-1)+CycleTime@k)`. Using `Y` previous maybe. But can use `X` for next? `G((normal -> X(runtime = runtime + CycleTime)))` if normal at k then at k+1? Hmm not exact due scan semantics. Better not include complex runtime assertions if uncertain.
A3: `G(!THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID -> X(Slab_Fault_Counter = Slab_Fault_Counter))` tautology? No, X(counter=counter) tautology. Need compare current to next: `G(!THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID -> (Slab_Fault_Counter = X(Slab_Fault_Counter)))` means if invalid at current, next counter equals current. But invalid at current should not record in current, so current counter equal previous, not next. If invalid persists, next equal current. But transition invalid may next valid fault rise and increment, so not invariant. Not good.

Could include only observable safety invariants and one history size? History array always 5 entries. Maybe:
A1 invalid no alarm
A2 valid fault alarm
A3 alarm release? `G(THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID & !THICKNESS_FAULT & !THICKNESS_ALARM -> ...)` no.
Maybe formal assertions optional; can omit? The JSON key says optional list. But to be safe include few. Need not be exhaustive. Could include ones from LTL with port names:
- `G(!THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID -> !THICKNESS_ALARM)`
- `G(THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID & THICKNESS_FAULT -> THICKNESS_ALARM)`
- `G((THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID & THICKNESS_FAULT & !X(THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID & THICKNESS_FAULT)) -> X(Slab_Fault_Counter != Slab_Fault_Counter))`? Hmm counter inequality. This uses X previous? It says on next scan counter differs. But rising edge at current k, counter increment at current O[k]. If at current edge, O[k] counter incremented. To assert, need previous. Could use `X` if edge at k then at k+1 counter != previous? Not exact. Maybe use `G((THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID & THICKNESS_FAULT & !Y(THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID & THICKNESS_FAULT)) -> (Slab_Fault_Counter = Y(Slab_Fault_Counter) + 1))` using Y previous. LTL with Y is acceptable? It's temporal. But "over port names" okay. Need include Y maybe not specified. The supplied LTL uses `previous(...)`, so okay. Could include `previous`. But need valid JSON string escaping? Fine. Use `previous(...)`. Formula: `G((THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID & THICKNESS_FAULT & !previous(THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID & THICKNESS_FAULT)) -> (Slab_Fault_Counter = previous(Slab_Fault_Counter) + 1))` This is over ports. But previous of output. Good. However if counter overflow, outside. Fine.
- Runtime: `G((THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID & !THICKNESS_FAULT & CUTTING_RUN) -> (Slab_Runtime_Accumulator = previous(Slab_Runtime_Accumulator) + CycleTime))` But first invocation previous? Assumes initial. Could include. But comparison LTIME + TIME requires type. Formula string acceptable.
- No record on non-rise: `G(!(THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID & THICKNESS_FAULT & !previous(THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID & THICKNESS_FAULT)) -> (Slab_Fault_Counter = previous(Slab_Fault_Counter) & Slab_Fault_History = previous(Slab_Fault_History)))` But uses previous for initial. Might be okay. But maybe too complex. Need concise.

The formal assertions should be optional list. Could include 4 simple. Need ensure over declared port names. The user asks "formal_assertions: optional list of {"id": "A1", "formula": "G(...)"} temporal/invariant assertions over declared VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT port names". We can include those. Need not include internal hold. Use port names exactly. Good.

Need state_machine JSON structure. We can define:
"state_machine": {
  "states": [
    {"name":"S0_POWER_UP","description":"...", "entry_actions":[...]},
    ...
  ],
  "transitions": [
    {"from":"S0_POWER_UP","to":"S1_SIGNAL_INVALID","condition":"NOT THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID","actions":[...]},
    {"from":"S0_POWER_UP","to":"S2_VALID_NORMAL","condition":"THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID AND NOT THICKNESS_FAULT","actions":["..."]},
    {"from":"S0_POWER_UP","to":"S3_VALID_FAULT","condition":"THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID AND THICKNESS_FAULT","actions":["initialize if not already"]}
...
  ]
}
But if S0 only first scan, transitions. Need init at power-up. Could have S0 entry actions initialize. Then immediate transition. Good.

Need maybe state names reflect hold. Could have S2_VALID_NORMAL and S4_VALID_HOLD. Transitions list as above. Need include actions for each transition:
- On any entry to S1: `THICKNESS_ALARM_Internal := FALSE; holdActive := FALSE; AlarmHoldTimer.IN reset (via holdTimerEnable false); prevValidFault := FALSE;` no stats reset. But invalid doesn't clear counter/history/runtime. Good.
- On rising valid fault (could occur in S1->S3 or S2->S3 or S4->S3): record in stage 2 before transition? Need actions: increment counter, shift history, set holdActive true, holdRestart true. In S3 entry? If S3 persistent no new edge, no record. If S4->S3 due fault true, likely edge from previous false validFault? In S4 fault false previous, so yes edge. In S2->S3 edge. In S1->S3 valid after invalid: prevValidFault false due S1 entry, so edge. So on transition to S3 from any state when fault true, is it always edge? From S3 to S3 persistent no transition. From S1 invalid to S3 valid fault: edge yes. From S2/S4 to S3 edge yes. So action record on transition to S3. But what if S3? no transition. Good. But if state S0 to S3 maybe record? At power-up initial fault valid? Requirement: On each false-to-true transition. At power-up previous invalid false; if valid fault first scan, is that a false-to-true transition? Assumption "a valid fault after signal loss is a new occurrence." At power-up maybe counted? The LTL initial? Need think. If first invocation has valid fault true, previous validFault initial false, so rise true, record? Likely yes? But requirement 5 at power-up initialize counter/history zero; if first scan valid fault, should record? The rising edge from initial false to true occurs. Assumptions: "a valid fault after signal loss is a new occurrence." Power-up not signal loss? But prev false. The benchmark likely expects record on first valid fault if initial prev false? Hmm. Need decide. The atomic proposition `rise = valid AND fault AND NOT previous(valid AND fault)`. At k=0 previous? Initial previous validFault false. So if first scan valid fault, rise true. So record. But if S0 to S3 action should record? Could. But power-up initialization also sets counter zero before scan. Then record increments to 1 and history[0]=timestamp. Is that expected? Maybe yes per LTL. But requirement 5 says at power-up initialize fault count/history zero. That's pre-invocation initial observation, not after first scan. So yes first scan can record. Need include S0->S3 action record if rise. But if S0 transitions to S3 on valid fault, edge sampled stage 1 prev false, rise true. Stage 2 record. Good. But if S0 entry initializes then transition actions record. Fine.

But maybe state machine should not use S0 as actual for more than first scan. We can handle S0 as init pseudo-state, immediate transition. Good.

Need timers:
- `AlarmHoldTimer` TON, PT := T#500ms. IN := `THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID AND holdActive AND NOT holdRestart`. Reset conditions: invalid signal, power-up/init, release (holdActive false), fresh valid fault rise (holdRestart true for one scan resets/restarts), maybe if fault persists? No reset while persistent? If fault persists, holdActive true and timer runs. If timer Q true, alarm still on due fault. On fresh rise? No rise. If fault drops after Q, holdActive cleared in S2/S3 transition? Need state S3->S2 when Q true and fault false. But if fault persists, holdActive remains true and timer Q true. If fault later drops, S3->S2, holdActive clear. Good. Timer Q true. In S2 timer IN false? holdActive false, resets? TON with IN false resets Q and ET. Good.
- Need fresh rising trigger restarts the hold: on rise set `holdRestart := TRUE` for current scan, causing TON IN false (reset) in stage 3. Next scan holdRestart false, IN true, timer starts from zero. Does this hold at least 500ms after edge? Edge scan timer reset; next scan starts. Alarm on due fault. If fault drops next scan, holdActive true, timer starts from zero next scan. Expiry 500ms after next scan. Good. But if fault drops on same edge scan? Not possible because edge fault true. Good.
- Could use `holdRestart` as reset condition. Need mention PT 500ms exact, time base ms. Reset on invalid, init, fresh rise, and when holdActive false. Maybe reset on release. Good.

Need priorities:
- Safety: invalid signal highest, forces alarm off and hold clear, no stats records/runtime add. Persistent valid fault forces alarm on. Statistics never affect permissives. History read-only. Then operational: rising valid fault record before alarm hold; hold minimum; runtime accumulation only normal. Need list.

Need initial_values:
- state S0_POWER_UP
- THICKNESS_ALARM false
- Slab_Fault_Counter 0
- Slab_Runtime_Accumulator "LTIME#0ns"
- Slab_Fault_History [0,0,0,0,0]
- internal: prevValidFault false, holdActive false, holdRestart false, AlarmHoldTimer reset (Q false, ET T#0ms), FaultCounter_Int 0, RuntimeAccumulator_Int LTIME#0ns, FaultHistory_Int [0,0,0,0,0]
Could include validFault false, validFaultRise false.
Need maybe `Slab_Fault_History_Internal` etc.

Need scan_execution_order explicit 4-stage. It must be array of 4 strings or objects. Need explicitly label:
1. Edge sampling: sample all inputs into scan-local values; compute `validFault := THICKNESS_SIGNAL_VALID AND THICKNESS_FAULT`; compute `validFaultRise := validFault AND NOT prevValidFault`; update `prevValidFault := validFault` (or stage 2? Need decide). But if invalid, stage 1 updates prev false. Good. Also sample `CycleTime`, `FaultTimestamp`.
2. Safety/reset priority & state transitions: FIRST apply invalid signal override (alarm off, holdActive false, holdRestart false, timer reset request, no record/runtime); then if invalid, state S1 and skip stats. Else evaluate state transitions. On `validFaultRise`, record fault (increment counter, shift history [4]:= [3]... [0]:= FaultTimestamp), set holdActive true, holdRestart true, alarm on. If persistent fault, alarm on. If fault absent and hold active, maintain until timer Q. If normal condition, add CycleTime to runtime internal. Update holdActive clear when timer Q and fault absent.
